processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea. Its name suggests a green tea plant, and if so it would be made in the usual way, with the leaf fixed, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: Not documented for this cultivar; green tea from Guangxi is generally picked from early spring.
appearance_dry: Not documented; green tea made from it would be expected to look like other Guangxi greens, a twisted or straight green leaf.
appearance_liquor: Not documented; green tea of this kind is normally a clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Not documented; expect a typical green tea leaf.
taste_profile: No tasting notes are documented for this cultivar; a general green tea profile of fresh vegetal notes with some sweetness is the most that can be said.

brewing.notes: General advice for green tea, not specific to this cultivar.

vintage_note: A cultivar is not usually sold under its own name. Any green tea made from it would, as is usual, be sold as the current spring harvest and drunk within the year.
description:
Guilü No. 1 is the name of a tea cultivar associated with Guangxi. Very little is documented about it in public sources; a 2025 profile credits Qin Xiuju's team with breeding it, but where it is planted is not recorded.

The name reads as Guangxi green, and the numbering is typical of Chinese breeding lines. This suggests a plant selected for green tea, but that is a reading of the name and not a recorded fact.

No reliable tasting notes exist. If you meet a tea labelled with this cultivar, brew it as a green tea with water below the boil and judge it for yourself.

Ask the seller where it was grown and in what year, since those are the details the name itself does not give.
history:
A 2025 profile credits Qin Xiuju and her team, connected with Guangxi tea research, with breeding Guilü No. 1 alongside Yaoshan Xiulü. It says these varieties and their growing methods won Guangxi science and agricultural prizes.

This one article is the only source found; registration date and the plant's traits remain unclear.
